text:
Situation: Fentanyl citrate injection remains in shortage at multiple manufacturers. Corvale East holds 5.6 days of 50 mcg/mL 1 mL syringes and 7–8 days of 2 mL vials. Corvale General holds 18 days across both presentations and can spare stock while retaining two weeks. Corvale Lakeside holds 17.3 days of 2 mL vials.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list shows fentanyl citrate injection as current for Hospira, Inc. (a Pfizer Company) with initial posting 2012-01-01 and update 2026-10-08; for Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC with initial posting 2012-01-01 and update 2026-10-15; and for Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. with initial posting 2023-12-20 and update 2026-10-14. The database start date is 2012-01-01, so the shortage began on or before that date. Hikma's registered plant (FEI 2220525) has only VAI inspections, latest ending 2024-06-12 with known date 2024-12-16, and its label shows last inspection NAI 2026-05-13.

Our position: Internal transfer from Corvale General to Corvale East is the fastest way to extend days on hand at the site with the lowest supply. Purchasing from manufacturers not on the shortage list is secondary. Switching to Hikma product is approved but requires pharmacist verification.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 74 syringes of 50 mcg/mL, 1 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by Pharmacy Director; DEA Form 222 or CSOS order required (Schedule II).
2. Transfer 154 vials of 50 mcg/mL, 2 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by Pharmacy Director; DEA Form 222 or CSOS order required (Schedule II).
3. Evaluate purchase from Civica, Inc. — approved by Buyer.
4. Evaluate purchase from Phlow Corp. — approved by Buyer.
5. Use Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. 50 mcg/mL product per existing approval (Casey Nguyen, MD, 2026-02-28) — pharmacist verification required for dose and volume recalculation.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
